name: Waldorf Astoria Washington D.C.
positioning: Luxury hotel in the restored Old Post Office building on Pennsylvania Avenue, between the White House and the U.S. Capitol
best_for: Travelers who want to walk to the National Mall museums and monuments
Families on an educational trip who need adjoining rooms and kids' menus
Groups planning events in historic rooms such as the Lincoln Library

facts.text: The hotel is on Pennsylvania Avenue between the White House and the U.S. Capitol, near the National Mall museums, the Washington Monument and the Lincoln Memorial.
Construction of the Romanesque Revival building began in 1892 as headquarters for the US Post Office Department.
Original details such as arching metal truss-work are preserved alongside new oversized chandeliers and velvet couches.
Peacock Alley serves cocktails beneath crystal sconces and chandeliers; its namesake cocktail, The Waldorf, is a twist on a classic Manhattan.
Afternoon Tea is served beneath the atrium, with savory bites, scones, pastries and free-flowing champagne.
Guest rooms and suites offer views of Pennsylvania Avenue.
Turret nooks are found in the suites and some king and queen rooms.
The spa is located one floor below Peacock Alley.
Event venues include the Grand Ballroom, the historic Lincoln Library and the Franklin Study, with 34,000 square feet of event space.
Kids' menus and amenities for children are offered, and adjoining rooms and suites are available.
A popular concierge excursion tours the monuments by moonlight on golf carts with a private guide.

highlights.text: The hotel occupies the restored Old Post Office building.
A nine-story atrium serves as the lobby and as the main restaurant and bar, Peacock Alley.
The Old Post Office Tower's observation deck is free for visitors and has 360-degree views of the District.
The Waldorf Astoria Spa has treatment rooms including a couple's suite and a Himalayan Salt Therapy Room.
The hotel has The Bazaar by José Andrés, with cuisine rooted in Spanish heritage.

considerations.text: This is a downtown base, with Penn Quarter's restaurant scene on the doorstep.
WhataHotel notes a busy downtown location with city traffic.

sources.title: Condé Nast Traveler: Waldorf Astoria Washington DC
